# DOC 01 // SPECIMENS [color=#FF3B30][bold]COMPANY CONFIDENTIAL :: SPECIAL PROJECTS :: EYES ONLY[/bold][/color]
- FROM: Office of the Director, Special Projects Group, Research and Development - TO: Corporate Liaisons, frontier postings, Neroid sector list B - REF: WY-SPG/0419-K - RE: Revised priority for biological specimen recovery
Effective on receipt, recovery of intact biological specimens of non-terrestrial origin supersedes all other liaison objectives at list B postings, including production quotas, contract renewals and personnel retention.
The Division's interest is in organisms of [bold]Class Black[/bold]: those showing parasitic reproduction, accelerated growth, collective behaviour, or chemistry hazardous to standard containment. Field reports of a corrosive blood agent, and of a sporulating growth that passes ordinary filtration, are of particular interest to [color=#3A3A36]##########[/color] at the Bio-Weapons Applications Office.
## HANDLING - Specimens are to be recovered alive where possible. A live specimen is valued at approximately forty times a preserved one. - Where a specimen is found inside a living host, the host is to be sedated and shipped in stasis with the specimen in place. The host is not to be informed. - No specimen is to be destroyed by colonial authorities, garrison forces or Colonial Marines. Liaisons will delay, misdirect or countermand any such order by whatever means are available.
## APPLICATIONS The Office has requested no fewer than three viable samples this fiscal year. A weapon that breeds itself costs nothing to stockpile and cannot be traced to a factory.
## COMPENSATION A recovery bonus of eighteen months' salary and transfer to a core world posting of the liaison's choosing. A liaison who fails to report a known specimen is in breach of contract.
[color=#6FA8FF][italic]Our note: list B is every colony in the sector with a garrison too small to say no. Check whether yours is on it. We think it is.[/italic][/color]
